description: Enterprise entity relational schema for the Celerey backend. Build these tables alongside the core users table. PostgreSQL recommended. All IDs are UUIDs.
note: This schema covers only the enterprise-specific tables. The full users table is maintained separately — only the enterprise-relevant columns are shown here for reference.

companies.description: An enterprise company that sponsors Celerey seat-based access for its employees. Created by a Celerey admin.

columns.contact_email: VARCHAR(255)  NOT NULL UNIQUE — primary billing / admin contact
columns.seat_limit: INTEGER       NOT NULL DEFAULT 10 — maximum number of active seats this company can have
columns.seats_used: INTEGER       NOT NULL DEFAULT 0  — trigger-maintained running count of active seats
columns.is_active: BOOLEAN       NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE — set FALSE to suspend all company seats
columns.notes: TEXT          NULL — internal Celerey admin notes

company_seats.description: Join table linking an individual user to an enterprise company. A user may only hold one active seat at a time. Supports pre-provisioning (invite by email before the user has registered).

columns.company_id: UUID          NOT NULL REFERENCES companies(company_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
columns.user_id: UUID          NULL     REFERENCES users(user_id) ON DELETE SET NULL — NULL until the invited user completes registration
columns.invite_email: VARCHAR(255)  NOT NULL — the email the seat was provisioned for; used as the natural key for pre-provisioned seats
columns.invite_accepted_at: TIMESTAMPTZ   NULL     — set when the user registers and links their account to this seat
columns.seat_granted_by: VARCHAR(255)  NULL     — admin name or email for audit trail
columns.seat_revoked_at: TIMESTAMPTZ   NULL     — NULL = still active; set to NOW() on revocation

constraints: UNIQUE (user_id) WHERE is_active = TRUE AND user_id IS NOT NULL — a user can only be on one active seat at a time
UNIQUE (company_id, invite_email) WHERE is_active = TRUE — no duplicate active seats for the same email within a company

triggers.after_seat_activated: AFTER INSERT or UPDATE SET is_active = TRUE  → INCREMENT companies.seats_used WHERE company_id = NEW.company_id
triggers.after_seat_deactivated: AFTER UPDATE SET is_active = FALSE            → DECREMENT companies.seats_used WHERE company_id = NEW.company_id

users_enterprise_columns.description: These columns must exist on the core users table. Shown here for reference — not a standalone table.

columns.user_type: VARCHAR(20)   NOT NULL DEFAULT 'regular' CHECK (user_type IN ('regular', 'enterprise'))
columns.subscription_status: VARCHAR(20)   NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none'    CHECK (subscription_status IN ('none', 'trialing', 'active'))

users_enterprise_columns.note: When a seat is granted: set user_type = 'enterprise' AND subscription_status = 'active'. When a seat is revoked: set user_type = 'regular' AND subscription_status = 'none'.

relationships.description: A company has many seats (active and historical)
A user can have at most one active seat at any point in time
Historical seats (is_active = FALSE) are retained for audit — a user may have had seats at multiple companies over time

v_active_company_seats.description: Convenience view: all active seats with company and user details — use this for the admin seat management screen
sql: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_active_company_seats AS
CASE WHEN cs.user_id IS NULL THEN 'pending' ELSE 'active' END AS seat_status
JOIN companies c ON c.company_id = cs.company_id
LEFT JOIN users u ON u.user_id = cs.user_id

v_company_summary.description: Per-company seat usage summary — use this for the admin companies list
sql: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW v_company_summary AS
COUNT(cs.seat_id) FILTER (WHERE cs.is_active = TRUE AND cs.user_id IS NOT NULL)  AS confirmed_seats,
COUNT(cs.seat_id) FILTER (WHERE cs.is_active = TRUE AND cs.user_id IS NULL)      AS pending_invites,
LEFT JOIN company_seats cs ON cs.company_id = c.company_id

steps: 1. Check companies.seats_used < companies.seat_limit — return 409 if at capacity

3a. If user exists: INSERT company_seats (company_id, user_id, invite_email, invite_accepted_at = NOW(), seat_granted_by); UPDATE users SET user_type = 'enterprise', subscription_status = 'active' WHERE user_id = :userId
3b. If user does not exist: INSERT company_seats (company_id, user_id = NULL, invite_email, seat_granted_by); send invite email; user links account on registration (see linkSeatOnRegistration)

linkSeatOnRegistration.description: Called when a pre-provisioned user completes sign-up
steps: 1. After user row is created, look up company_seats WHERE invite_email = new user's email AND is_active = TRUE AND user_id IS NULL
2. If found: UPDATE company_seats SET user_id = :newUserId, invite_accepted_at = NOW()
3. UPDATE users SET user_type = 'enterprise', subscription_status = 'active' WHERE user_id = :newUserId

revokeSeat.description: Remove enterprise access from a user
steps: 1. UPDATE company_seats SET is_active = FALSE, seat_revoked_at = NOW() WHERE seat_id = :seatId
2. UPDATE users SET user_type = 'regular', subscription_status = 'none' WHERE user_id = :userId

suspendCompany.description: Suspend all users for a company (e.g. non-payment)
steps: 1. UPDATE companies SET is_active = FALSE WHERE company_id = :companyId
2. UPDATE users SET user_type = 'regular', subscription_status = 'none' WHERE user_id IN (SELECT user_id FROM company_seats WHERE company_id = :companyId AND is_active = TRUE AND user_id IS NOT NULL)
3. Note: company_seats rows remain intact so the company can be re-activated without re-provisioning

sampleQueries.checkIfUserHasActiveSeat: SELECT cs.*, c.company_name FROM company_seats cs JOIN companies c ON c.company_id = cs.company_id WHERE cs.user_id = ':userId' AND cs.is_active = TRUE LIMIT 1
sampleQueries.companiesNearSeatLimit: SELECT * FROM v_company_summary WHERE seats_used >= seat_limit * 0.9 AND is_active = TRUE
sampleQueries.pendingInvitesOlderThan7Days: SELECT * FROM company_seats WHERE user_id IS NULL AND is_active = TRUE AND seat_granted_at < NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
